answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by pricing extra identities along a rising stake spiral: the first persona posts a modest bond, but each added alias must lock more than the sum of all earlier bonds under the same controller. Each epoch a public beacon publishes independent countersignatures from already-established peers, not from siblings in one cluster. Spendable rewards unlock only after a claimant clears a reputation ridge of enough distinct attestors and no near-duplicate answers. Mass registration then fails, because those escalating costs outrun what a cloned fleet can recoup.
